observation.description: The documented Expo path (guide clients/react-expo.md: same @expo/snapback-client + @expo/snapback-react as web) cannot establish a session on a stock Expo SDK 57 / RN 0.86 app: React Native/Hermes provides no globalThis.crypto, and the packaged client requires crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256') (react-binding.mjs manifest digests), crypto.getRandomValues (mutation identity), and crypto.randomUUID (provider/store ids). prepareReactBinding dies with "Cannot read property 'subtle' of undefined". Neither the guide page nor the package documents any polyfill requirement; the arm proceeded only after authoring an expo-crypto-backed WebCrypto shim (evidence/app/src/crypto-polyfill.ts).

competitorOutcome.description: The Firebase JS SDK runs on React Native out of the box (RN is a documented first-class environment; no WebCrypto prerequisite for auth/Firestore basics).

mustNotRegress: The digest-bound binding verification itself (manifest identity checks) - fix the primitive's availability, not the verification.
smallestCoherentFix: Ship an RN-safe crypto seam in the client: pure-JS SHA-256 fallback for the binding digests when subtle is absent, an explicit refusal naming the missing primitive for getRandomValues/randomUUID (or a documented one-line expo-crypto adapter), plus a react-expo guide prerequisites note.
acceptanceWitness: A fresh Expo SDK 57 app on the documented path reaches a ready provider and a live query against the packaged closure with zero consumer-authored polyfills (or fails with a named SNAPBACK_* diagnostic pointing at the documented adapter).
